A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PPGT research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F are readable and matchable despite additions and substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original BREC expressivity results, graph benchmark evaluations, architectural ablations, normalization experiments, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds PASCALVOC-SP and OGBN-ArXiv evaluations.

M1.justification: AdaRMSN, simplified L2 attention, URPE, and the sinusoidal PE stem remain unchanged. v3 adds a task-specific adaptation for OGBN-ArXiv: BFS-based Node2Subgraph conversion, a class-attention prediction head, and dual-direction RRWP features (Sections 3.3, 5.3, and A.4).

E1.justification: v3 adds PASCALVOC-SP superpixel semantic segmentation and OGBN-ArXiv transductive node classification on a large citation graph. These substantially extend the represented domains, prediction requirements, and input-size scenarios. The earlier benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: LRGB Table 3 adds DRew and Exphormer while removing CKGCN, Transformer+LapPE, both SAN variants, and GMLP-Mixer from that comparison. New Table 5 compares PPGT against GCN, GCN-NSampler, DeeperGCN, SIGN, NodeFormer, SGFormer, and Exphormer on OGBN-ArXiv. Comparator membership in Tables 1, 2, and 4 is retained.

E3.justification: New evaluation procedures include OGBN-ArXiv BFS subgraphs capped at 100 nodes, a node-masking setting of 0.5, and PASCALVOC-SP F1 evaluation with its own training configuration. v3 also reports adopting the updated LRGB setup of Tönshoff et al. (2024). The unchanged retained PPGT scores and hyperparameters do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 4 retains the same ZINC architectural ablations. Appendix B retains the SPE-basis sensitivity study, normalization reconstruction case study, batch-size sensitivity analysis, and runtime/memory comparison. Section 5.5 summarizes these existing studies without adding an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions use four-seed mean and standard-deviation reporting, specify seeds 0–3, report a single PCQM4Mv2 run, and retain the one-tailed 5% t-test discussion. The new benchmark results extend the existing uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds PPGT results of 0.4641 ± 0.0033 F1 on PASCALVOC-SP and 72.46 ± 0.15 accuracy on OGBN-ArXiv. LRGB baseline scores are revised under the reported updated setup; for example, GCN Peptides-Function AP changes from 0.5930 to 0.6860. BREC, Benchmarking GNNs, PCQM4Mv2, and PPGT's peptide scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Table 1 refines N2GNN's theoretical classification: v2 gives an unnamed class bounded by 3-FWL, whereas v3 identifies 2-FWL+ and adds its relation to 2-FWL. The PPGT expressivity proof, normalization-invariance proof, and associated propositions and lemma in Appendix E are retained.

C1.justification: The central three-component PPGT contribution and graph-learning claims remain. Section 6 adds the limited prospective claim that the architectural insights may benefit Transformers outside graph domains. The multimodal-unification motivation emphasized in v3's abstract was already present in v2.

C2.justification: v3 adds an interpretation of URPE-equipped PPGT as CKGConv with a dynamic density function, explicitly identifies PE design as an expressivity bottleneck, and discusses balancing expressivity against node coverage on large graphs. The original magnitude-preservation explanation and quadratic-complexity limitation remain, with sampling now discussed as a mitigation.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a detailed PCQM4Mv2 configuration in Table 9, where v2 primarily referred to GRIT's configuration. It also documents OGBN-ArXiv sampling and model settings, adds PASCALVOC-SP hyperparameters, and discloses Edge-dim values for retained experiments. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing changes to the retained runs.

R1.justification: Section 4 substantially expands positioning through dedicated discussions of CKGConv and Transformer universality, a more explicit comparison with TokenGT, and additional literature on approximation and graph expressivity. The new large-graph discussion adds comparisons with efficiency-oriented Transformers and references on graph sampling.

P1.justification: The overall section and appendix organization is retained. Targeted edits revise the abstract, related-work discussion, and conclusion; PCQM4Mv2 moves into a dedicated large-scale evaluation subsection, Further Study becomes Section 5.5, and terminology and typographical errors are corrected. Much of the original exposition remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document template, typography, margins, author layout, and display placement throughout. Previously wrapped figures become standalone displays, and the side-by-side LRGB/PCQM4Mv2 tables are separated. It also adds the OGBN-ArXiv results and large-benchmark configuration tables and expands existing tables with dataset columns and parameter rows.

improvement.justification: The new segmentation and sampled large-graph evaluations broaden empirical support, while the expanded configuration tables improve reproducibility, particularly for PCQM4Mv2. These provide useful incremental gains. A new reporting inconsistency tempers the improvement: Section 5.2 still calls GRIT the best Peptides-Function model, although revised Table 3 gives DRew higher AP, 0.7150 versus 0.6988.
